w_p1: TubeCutter downloads YouTube videos and trims them to the exact section you choose. Paste a link, set In and Out on the timeline, and add the cut to the download queue.
w_p2: This installer puts TubeCutter in your Applications folder and opens it. It takes less than a minute.
w_li1: Click Continue through the next screens, then Install. Your Mac asks for your password once.
w_li2: TubeCutter opens by itself when it is done.
w_muted: Needs macOS 11 (Big Sur) or newer on a Mac with Apple silicon.
r_p: Some videos only open for a signed-in viewer. TubeCutter can use its own YouTube sign-in or borrow one from your browser. Nothing is sent anywhere except to YouTube.
r_b_1: Open Account & Settings in TubeCutter and press 1. Sign in to Google, then 2. Connect YouTube.
r_b_2: Close that window, then choose App's YouTube session under Download authentication. No extra permission is needed.
r_b_3: Or choose Chrome, Firefox, Opera or Safari there instead: macOS may ask for Keychain or Full Disk Access.
r_o_1: Leave Download authentication on Anonymous. Many public videos work without an account.
r_end: Then paste a video link, press Analyze, and choose what to download.
c_p: TubeCutter is in your Applications folder, and it is opening now.
c_trash_h: If your Mac can't move the installer to the Trash
c_trash: That happens when an earlier TubeCutter-Installer.dmg is already in the Trash. It's harmless: click OK, then delete TubeCutter-Installer.dmg from Downloads.
d_subtitle: TubeCutter isn't from the App Store, so your Mac stops the installer once. To let it through:
d_step2: A message says it can't be opened. Click **Done** (not Move to Trash).
d_step3: Double-click the blue button below. In the page that opens, scroll to the bottom and click **Open Anyway**.
d_step4: Confirm with **Open Anyway** and your password. The installer opens: click **Continue**, then **Install**.
d_footnote: On macOS 13 or 14 it's quicker: right-click the installer, choose **Open**, then **Open** again.
